paper_metadata.title: Microstructural evolution and high-temperature strengthening mechanisms of the IN 738LC superalloy prepared by selective laser melting
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology

evidence.quote: The IN 738LC superalloy is a typical precipitation-strengthened nickel-based superalloy
IN 738LC alloys fabricated using different additive processes and casting

Defect-free SLM-IN 738LC superalloy samples were fabricated using selective laser melting (SLM). The as-built samples exhibit a cellular structure with fine carbides, γ′ phases, and high-density dislocations at the cell boundary and nano-size γ′ phases in the interior
the samples were fabricated under a hatch spacing of 0.1 mm, a powder layer thickness of 50 μm, a scanning speed ranging from 600 to 1400 mm/s, and a laser power ranging from 150 to 300 W
The as-built samples were first subjected to solution heat treatment (SHT) at 1020 ◦C, 1070 ◦C, 1120 ◦C, 1160 ◦C, and 1200 ◦C for 2 h followed by air cooling (AC)
and then underwent aging heat treatment (AHT) at 845 ◦C for 24 h followed by AC.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure analysis of the HT samples
evidence.quote: When the SHT temperature is increased to 1070 ◦C (Fig. 5 (b)), a bimodal distribution of γ′ phases becomes obvious. The coarse γ′ phases, with a cuboidal shape, have an average diameter of ~321.3 nm, whereas the fine spherical γ′ phases of ~51.6 nm.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure analysis of the HT samples
evidence.quote: The samples subjected to 1120 + AHT also display a bimodal distribution (Fig. 5 (c)), with coarse and fine γ′ phases coarsening. The coarse γ′ phases have an average diameter of ~480.4 nm, while the fine γ′ phases are of ~87.8 nm.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure analysis of the HT samples

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure analysis of the HT samples
evidence.quote: the EDS analysis (Fig. 6 (a)) revealed the presence of coarse blocky phases enriched in Ti, Nb, Ta, and C, as well as fine strip phases enriched with Cr and C at the grain boundaries. Further electron diffraction analysis (Fig. 6 (b)) confirmed the existence of three distinct phases: the γ matrix, γ′ phases, and M23C6 carbides.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure analysis of the HT samples
evidence.quote: Overall, the grain boundaries after HT contain blocky MC carbide, slender M23C6 carbide, and γ′ phases.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure analysis of the HT samples
evidence.quote: The presence of γ′ phases, which are coherent with the γ matrix, induces lattice distortions within the cellular structure. This contributes to the favorable mechanical properties of the as-built samples.
This is attributed to the synergistic strengthening effect of the bimodal distribution of the γ′ phase.

When the temperature increased to 800–900 ◦C, the dislocations shearing γ′ phases is activated and the alloy remained high strength. At 1000 ◦C, both the dislocation shearing and dislocation bypassing mechanisms coexist
At 1000 ◦C, both the dislocation shearing and dislocation bypassing mechanisms coexist, resulting in a decrease in the strength of the alloy and an increase in its plasticity.
